title: MATLAB for Chicken Behaviors
author: Alireza Abdoli
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcacisaw

steps.title: Initial MATLAB Setup
steps.instruction: Prepare the MATLAB environment to ensure function and data visibility.

substeps.instruction: Download the required data and function files.
Change the MATLAB path to the folder containing the downloaded data and files.
Open an instance of the MATLAB program.

steps.title: Slice Large CSV Files using daySlicer
steps.instruction: Break large CSV files into smaller, day-long MAT files for easier processing.

substeps.instruction: Place the 'daySlicer.m' function in the same folder as the CSV files.
Change the MATLAB path to this folder.
Invoke the function using the syntax: daySlicer('starting_time-stamp', number_of_days).
Example: daySlicer('2018-03-29 00:00:00', 11) to extract 11 days starting from 2018-03-29.
Note: Use the European date format (yyyy-mm-dd) for the timestamp.
Verify that a new folder with the same name as the CSV file has been created containing the MAT files.

steps.title: Extract Data Chunks using chicklet
steps.instruction: Extract specific smaller chunks of data (minutes or hours) from a CSV file.

substeps.instruction: Place the 'chicklet.m' function in the same folder as the CSV file.
Change the MATLAB path to this folder.
Invoke the function using the syntax: chicklet('starting_time-stamp', minutes_to_extract, recording_frequency).
Note: The recording frequency is optional and defaults to 100Hz.
Select the input CSV file when prompted by the window.
Locate the resulting CSV file in the original folder (the filename will include the initial timestamp).

steps.title: Classify Behaviors using behaviorSearch
steps.instruction: Identify pecking, preening, and dustbathing behaviors within a prepared chicken dataset.

substeps.instruction: Create a new folder and move the 'behaviorSearch.m' function and the target data files into it.
Change the MATLAB path to this new folder.
Load the data file into MATLAB by dragging it from the Current Folder onto the Command Window.
Invoke the function using the syntax: labels = behaviorSearch(chicken_timeseries), where 'chicken_timeseries' is the 3D (X, Y, Z axis) time series.
Interpret the output vector: 0 = non-behavior, 2 = pecking, 3 = preening, 4 = dustbathing.

steps.title: Visualize Behavior Results
steps.instruction: Plot the identified behavior labels over the original time series data for visual verification.

substeps.instruction: Run the command: plot(chicken_timeseries) to plot X (Blue), Y (Orange), and Z (Red) axes.
Run the command: hold on to allow overlay plotting.
Run the command: plot(labels) to plot the behavior regions in purple.
